Abdur-Rahman bin Auf, under a written pact with Umaiya bin Khalaf, tries to shield him at Badr, but Bilal calls the Ansar, who kill Umaiya and his son.
In his tent at Badr, in armour, the Prophet pleads for Allah's promise until Abu Bakr says it is enough, then goes out reciting that the multitude will be routed.
Warned by Sa'd, Umaiya bin Khalaf is urged out by Abu Jahl and killed at Badr; Ka'b missed Badr unblamed; al-Miqdad pledges to fight; the Prophet appeals to Allah.
Al-Bara and Ibn Umar were too young for Badr, whose warriors numbered over three hundred and ten, like the believers who crossed the river with Saul.
The Prophet invokes evil on Quraysh leaders, later seen dead; Ibn Mas'ud finds Abu Jahl dying, struck down by the two sons of Afra, and hears his last words.
The verse on two disputing opponents came down about six who fought at Badr: Hamza, Ali, Ubaida, Shaiba, Utba and al-Walid; Ali duelled in two armours.
Umaiya and his son die at Badr; an old man who would not prostrate is later killed as a disbeliever; Az-Zubair's Badr and Yarmuk wounds and his dented, silver-decorated sword.
The Prophet addresses the Quraysh dead thrown into a Badr well, saying they hear him; Aisha says his words were that they now know, and Ibn Abbas explains verse 14:28.
Haritha, martyred at Badr, is in Firdaus; Hatib, a Badr warrior, is spared over his letter; arrows are used sparingly; Badr and Uhud losses; Afra's sons knock down Abu Jahl.
Badr's warriors and angels are ranked the best; Gabriel came armed; Badr men in other reports: a widow's remarriage after childbirth, sacrifice meat after three days, Az-Zubair's spear.
Reports naming Badr warriors: Ubada's pledge, Abu Hudhaifa adopting Salim, a wedding lament for a Badr father, angels avoiding dogs and pictures, drunk Hamza maiming Ali's camels, Hafsa's remarriage.

Reports naming Badr warriors: spending on family as charity, Gabriel offering five prayers at fixed hours, al-Baqara's last two verses, renting fields, Bahrain's jizya, fear of wealth, sparing house snakes.
Abbas's ransom is not waived; a foe professing Islam must be spared; Abu Jahl dies; Badr warriors' stipends and booty shares; the first civil strife leaves none of them alive.
At Badr Al-Miqdad told the Prophet they would not speak as the Children of Israel spoke to Moses but would go on with him, which greatly delighted the Prophet.
Ibn Abbas said Surat Al-Anfal was revealed concerning the Battle of Badr.
The verse on two opponents disputing about their Lord was revealed about those who went out to fight at Badr, Ali, Hamza and Ubaida against Utba, Shaiba and Al-Walid.
At Badr the Prophet pleads for Allah's promise until Abu Bakr stops him, then recites that their multitude will flee; Aisha recalls 54.46 coming at Mecca in her childhood.
